rows.exact_frozen_ssc_body: In W04c, Wick rotation becomes a gauge-like extra choice, and the left chiral symmetry is interpreted internally before that choice. Its Wick rotation is described as LIKE a gauge choice, breaking the left chiral symmetry after choosing a CP1 fibration/imaginary-time normal direction; the source does not establish a literal physical gauge-equivalence operation.

W04c leaves the electroweak/Higgs completion of the revised viewpoint unresolved. The March 10 post expressly says large parts of the physical construction are missing: the author has made slow progress, does not here develop quantum gravity, and continues to work out how to formulate the proposed holomorphic quantum field theory. These are dated source-negative completion claims, not proof of impossibility.

W04c promotes the PT+/PT-/null-orbit holomorphic/boundary picture from an analogy to the proposed fundamental starting point, while stating that a gravitational theory must abandon or deform the global SU(2,2) structure. The source gives PT as three complex dimensional with open components PT+ and PT- meeting on a common boundary N of five real dimensions; Minkowski spacetime is encoded through CP1s contained inside N, in an inherently chiral framework acknowledged as Penrose's parity/googly problem. Positive and negative energy/time holomorphy in upper/lower half planes is presented as the analogue of PT+/PT- holomorphic data with hyperfunction boundary data on N. It distinguishes SU(2,2) conformal symmetry on standard CP3 from the smaller Poincare group and asserts that a gravity theory must abandon the global SU(2,2) description in favor of holomorphic CP1s embedded in a more general complex threefold. These are source-scoped geometrical and proposed-gravity claims, not a construction of quantum gravity.

W04c interprets Wick rotation as an extra choice of CP1 fibration/imaginary-time direction rather than a fundamental Euclidean-to-Minkowski coordinate substitution. For QM the author defines the Wick-rotation picture as choosing positive-imaginary-axis real analytic restriction of an upper-complex-time-half-plane holomorphic object instead of its hyperfunction boundary values on real time. In the twistor analogy a Wick rotation requires choosing a CP1 fibration of PT and an imaginary-time direction NORMAL TO the real three-dimensional family of fibration fibers on N; this is not mere equality of real-time and imaginary-time coordinates.

W04c explicitly revises the Euclidean-first program into a Minkowski-twistor/holomorphic-first viewpoint and treats Euclidean geometry as a chosen realization of more primitive complex-twistor data. The post distinguishes the earlier Euclidean-first viewpoint (PT as complex structures on tangent spaces of a real four-manifold, deriving Minkowski after imaginary-time choice) from the author's more recent March 10 proposed Minkowski-twistor/holomorphic-boundary-first viewpoint in which an arbitrary boundary-normal choice yields a real-analytic restriction. The author's March 12 comments separately qualify the preferred fundamental picture toward complex-time holomorphy, but those later replies do not silently rewrite this original post or prove its model.

In the revised W04c role assignment SL(2,C)_R acts on the twistor CP1 point data while the left factor acts on the tangent space to the space parametrizing the CP1s; after the Wick-rotation choice an SU(2)_L role is interpreted internally.

W04c proposes that the choice involved in Wick rotation can break the internal SU(2)_L role, but explicitly says the complete electroweak/Higgs formalism has not been recovered. W04c explicitly says a consistent ordinary-spacetime electroweak/Higgs formalism from the proposed Wick-choice/internal-SU2L construction is NEEDED and the author does NOT KNOW HOW to obtain it; he calls the possibility not obviously impossible. No completed electroweak/Higgs reduction is claimed.

W04c retains Penrose and Penrose-Ward structures and proposes the canonical line and rank-three quotient bundles on CP3 as sources of U(1) and SU(3) internal structure, with matter described by holomorphic or Dolbeault-type data. W04c distinguishes the Penrose transform for Weyl-equation solutions described by holomorphic line-bundle sections over PT+ from the somewhat different Penrose-Ward self-dual gauge-field correspondence using holomorphic vector bundles over PT+. It separately discusses tangent-bundle SL2R action along CP1 fibers and SU2L action as not yet worked out, then the canonical line and rank-three complex quotient bundle on CP3 with source U1xU3 local symmetry and one projective U1 factor removed yielding the author's proposed U1xSU3. Matter is tentatively holomorphic sections on PT+, and the proposal says gauge couplings may be encoded by bundle holomorphic structure AT LEAST IN THE SELF-DUAL CASE, perhaps by Dolbeault-like operators; no fully interacting matter theory is supplied.

W04c leaves the generation problem, the correct Dirac-versus-Dolbeault operator, interacting dynamics, and much of the proposed holomorphic field theory unresolved. The author explicitly asks whether Dirac or Dolbeault operators are appropriate and how fermion generations arise. He also leaves a consistent interacting holomorphic quantum-field-theory implementation as challenging future work; these are source-explicit unresolved questions, not closure by a familiar named operator.
